## p7c Command

```bash
p7c -l -v
```
or equivalently:
```bash
p7c --list --verbose
```

## What the flags do

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `-l` / `--list` | Lists all modules currently loaded into the `%code` hash |
| `-v` / `--verbose` | Shows verbose output including module name, description, and metadata (not just module names) |

## Expected output

With `-l -v`, you get a table showing:

```
Loaded modules (coding zenka):
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Module Name   │ Description                          │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ zenka.coding.handler   │ Handles queued tasks for coding zenka │
│ zenka.coding.validator │ Validates code submissions            │
│ ...                 │ ...                                  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The **`-v` (verbose)** flag is the key one here — without it, `-l` only shows bare module names; with it, you see the full metadata (name, description, load time, etc.) from each module's header (`# name = X` and `# descr = Y`).
